correctness.rationale: For every alpha,d>0 and 0<q<d/(d+1), exact differentiation gives the double angular root at z*=(1-q)/alpha, h''(z*)=-alpha^2(d+1), radial rate -mu<0 and lambda'(z*)=-alpha(d+1)q. A forward-invariant small positive rectangle gives exponential u decay. Riccati comparison yields \(w=z-z_*=1/(\kappa t)+O(\log(t)/t^2)\), while the exponentially small forcing in the reciprocal-ratio equation is integrable. Integration of d(log u)/dt yields a finite positive amplitude and exponent nu=2q/(1-q). The strong stable eigendirection gives slope -z*/mu; b<d makes prey-only state hyperbolically stable. The actual packaged verify.py computed all symbolic identities and returned VERIFY_OK on numerical diagnostics; finite simulation does not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The ratio-fixed-point fold is an ecologically motivated boundary of the source's extinction regimes. The theorem establishes a physically observable mixed time scale: angular ratio decays as 1/t, abundances as exponential decline with the noninteger power \(t^{-\nu}\), with a separate pure-exponential stable trajectory; at \(b<d\) an open extinction basin coexists with prey-only stability exactly at the threshold. This informs basin/fate interpretation beyond counting fixed points or applying a generic saddle-node slogan.
